exposure: early pregnancy hemoglobin A1c (<20 weeks' gestation)
good glycemic control (early and late A1c <6.5%)
improved glycemic control (early A1c >6.5% and late A1c <6.5%)
outcome: large for gestational age weight at birth
cohort: Pregnancies complicated by pregestational diabetes from January 2012 to December 2016 at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center with both an early A1c (<20 weeks' gestation) and late A1c (>26 weeks' gestation) available for analysis.
finding: Strict glycemic control throughout pregnancy with a late pregnancy A1c target of <6.5% in pregnancies complicated by pregestational diabetes led to reduced rates of adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes.
